findings.title: Update error path records legacy duration instead of storage duration
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. The failure comes from the unified store, so this should be `recordStorageDuration`. The same slip is in Create at line 45. The metrics misattribute storage failures to legacy, and storage error metrics are never recorded.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records storage metric instead of legacy
findings.body: After the async `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)`. It should call `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors get folded into the storage metrics, which corrupts both series. Legacy delete-collection is never recorded as legacy.

findings.title: Delete uses d.Log instead of the enriched log for the context
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` drops the `name`, `kind` and `method` values built into `log`. Downstream logging then lacks that context. Every other method uses `log`.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses `name` as the kind label
findings.body: `recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object name where every other call passes `options.Kind`. This creates a Prometheus label value per object, which means unbounded cardinality, and it splits the series between success and error.

findings.title: Async goroutines reuse the request context and objects after the request returns
findings.body: The legacy write goroutines derive their context from the request `ctx`, which is cancelled once the HTTP request completes. The legacy write then races with the cancellation, so the 'safety' write to legacy can be cancelled and silently fail. Update also reuses `objInfo`, `createValidation` and `updateValidation` closures after the request has returned. These may capture request state, and the legacy update recomputes the object from the legacy store rather than using the updated result. The result is a non-deterministic legacy copy. A detached context (`context.WithoutCancel`) is needed. Create and Delete have the same problem.

findings.title: Redundant `return created, err`; legacy failures are never logged
findings.body: After the error check, `err` is always nil, so `return created, err` is misleading. In the goroutines (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection), legacy errors are only recorded in metrics and never logged. That makes the asynchronous legacy write hard to debug when it fails.

findings.title: Tests don't synchronize with or verify the async legacy writes
findings.body: The code launches goroutines that call the legacy mock. Tests neither wait for them nor assert that legacy was called or not called. The goroutines can run after the test finishes and race on the shared `mock.Mock`, which is not safe under `-race`. In the Delete and DeleteCollection tests no legacy mock is set up, so the goroutine calls an unmocked method, which panics in testify and can crash the test binary. The async behavior this PR introduces is effectively untested.
